Transferring experience to a shelf lift

A matched comparison shows how reports from related interactions help the agent complete a shelf-righting motion.

In this exampleThe comparisonThe shelf lift

We find that providing related experience, in the form of summaries of tested strategies, successes and failures, aids iterative refinement on a new task. Here, we investigate this through a walkthrough of G1 raising a shelf from its side to an upright position. The prior experience comes from four other furniture interactions, including carrying a table, lifting a chair, and pulling and pushing a chair.

We first run four Codex agents for 15 minutes and select the best valid motion. From this shared starting solution, we run two separate 15-minute continuations, one with the related experience and one without. Both receive equal time and compute budgets. This lets us examine exactly what the supplied experience changes during refinement.
